title: Coherent energy cascades in nonlinear disordered Hamiltonians
authors: Anxo Biasi, Brad Cownden, Oleg Evnin, Alvaro Iturbe Jabaloyes
abstract: The familiar wave kinetic theory revolves around turbulent energy cascades characterized by random phases of the individual normal modes. By contrast, recent years have revealed turbulent cascades where the transfer of energy is mediated by phase-coherent dynamics. Such coherent cascades have been previously established in deterministic systems with a tightly controlled algebraic structure of the mode interactions, such as nonlinear Schrödinger equations.   Here, we show that the presence of phase-coherent cascades is robust with respect to substantial alterations of the mode couplings. We prove that, in infinite-dimensional resonant Hamiltonian systems with fully resonant normal mode spectra and random nonlinear couplings, a structured subset of couplings --- an infinitesimal fraction of the total --- suffices to support coherent cascades characterized by phase alignment, the formation of power-law spectra, and either unbounded growth of Sobolev norms or a finite-time blow-up. Numerical simulations further demonstrate the emergence of coherent cascades from random initial data through a process of phase locking, suggesting a mechanism for their emergence in broader classes of initial data and systems. We thus show that disordered mode interactions can sustain, rather than block, coherent energy transport across arbitrarily distant scales.
summary: This work proves that phase-coherent energy cascades can persist in highly disordered, infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems. By showing that only an infinitesimal fraction of structured couplings is necessary, the authors demonstrate that organized structure can guide energy flow across many scales, even when the system is largely random. This challenges the notion that disorder necessarily destroys coherent energy transport.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mechanism of energy transfer (energy cascades) in nonlinear, dispersive Hamiltonian systems, specifically contrasting phase-incoherent (weak turbulence) versus phase-coherent energy transport.
main_result: Coherent energy cascades are robust and can be sustained even in systems with predominantly random nonlinear couplings, provided a small, structured subset of couplings remains organized.
method: The authors use theoretical proofs to construct resonant Hamiltonian systems that support invariant manifolds, followed by numerical simulations to test the robustness of the cascade mechanism.
model_or_system: The model is an infinite-dimensional resonant Hamiltonian system described by equations of motion involving random nonlinear couplings. The system conserves energy and particle number, and the analysis focuses on the dynamics near an invariant manifold.
key_observables: Phase alignment of normal modes, formation of power-law energy spectra ($E_n \propto n^{-\gamma}$), and the growth/blow-up of Sobolev norms ($H_s$).
important_parameters: The ratio of deterministic to random couplings, the spectral resonance structure, and the dimensionality of the system.
main_assumptions: The initial theoretical proofs are established on the assumption of an invariant manifold, though numerical work tests robustness outside this regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the three types of energy cascades (I, II, and III) and show the emergence of Cascade III from random initial data, confirming power-law formation and phase distribution.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a construction for resonant Hamiltonian systems supporting invariant manifolds, analyzes the resulting energy cascade solutions (categorizing them by spectral decay and norm growth), and concludes by proving the robustness of the coherent cascade mechanism against disorder.
why_interesting: The finding that structured interactions can survive and mediate energy transfer across vast scales in the presence of disorder is highly relevant to understanding complex, non-integrable quantum many-body systems where disorder is inherent.
